field_name: Multi-hop Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs

categories.name: Stepwise Reasoning and Decomposition
categories.description: Methods that decompose multi-hop questions into intermediate sub-questions with grounding on supporting facts for each reasoning step

categories.name: Iterative Retrieval-Augmented Generation
categories.description: RAG-based approaches that perform multiple retrieval iterations with summarization or planning to manage context and avoid over-planning

categories.name: Agentic Search and Planning
categories.description: Systems that use autonomous agents to dynamically plan and execute retrieval strategies over knowledge graphs

categories.name: Knowledge Rewriting and Reflection
categories.description: Frameworks that use reflection loops and structured knowledge operations to rewrite and refine knowledge representations for better reasoning

categories.name: Closed-loop Verification Systems
categories.description: Methods that incorporate backward consistency verification and unified memory to validate reasoning paths and prevent early commitment to incorrect paths

categories.name: Answer Post-processing and Correction
categories.description: Techniques that detect and correct problematic answers (e.g., off-topic, factual errors) through self-correction mechanisms

categories.name: Training Data Enrichment
categories.description: Approaches that enhance supervision signals by enriching training triples with contextual information from source passages

categories.name: Subgraph Retrieval Methods
categories.description: Techniques focused on retrieving relevant subgraphs from knowledge graphs to reduce reasoning space and improve interpretability

common_assumptions: Grounding on supporting facts or context improves reasoning accuracy
Iterative or stepwise processes allow for error correction and refinement
Unified models or joint optimization improve performance across reasoning steps
Efficiency metrics (token usage, computational cost) are important for practical deployment

repeated_limitations.description: Exposure bias between training and inference when predicted intermediate states deviate from ground truth
Context overload from multiple retrieval rounds or long contexts
Need for annotated evidence or decomposition supervision for training
High computational costs from knowledge graph construction or iterative processing
Limited generalization across different question types or domains

underexplored_combinations: Combining local context subgraph enrichment with adaptive repair loops for training data improvement
Integrating reinforcement learning optimization with context-aware training for transfer to deeper hops
Using closed-loop verification mechanisms in training data generation processes

contradictions.description: Whether iterative retrieval improves or hinders interpretability - some argue it reduces interpretability while others claim stepwise reasoning enhances it
